articles.title: ‘The Song of Scorpions,’ ‘Qissa’ Director Anup Singh Sets Mumbai Film ‘Lasya: The Gentle Dance’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Anup Singh, director of “Qissa” and “The Song of Scorpions,” is directing a new short film, “Lasya: The Gentle Dance,” shot on Mumbai’s streets, produced by Mumbai-based Pretty Pictures.
body: The film is produced by Pretty Pictures, the Mumbai-based banner helmed by Zeeshan Ahmad and Pretty Aggarwal.

“Anup Singh’s work has always been about people on the margins,” Ahmad said. “His cinema has consistently insisted that their life not be documented only for the pain, but that the joys and the beauty of their life also be affirmed. We would like to support that vision in our work together.”

Following the short, Pretty Pictures plans to begin work with Singh early next year on his next feature film, which would mark the third film he was set to make with Irrfan Khan. The project returns some six years after the actor’s death.

“After this short, we are ready to start working with Anup Singh on his next feature film early next year,” Ahmad said. “Anup Singh is finally ready to return to the film. We are very excited to make this film in homage to Irrfan Khan.”

articles.title: Shailene Woodley Was Crushed When She Found Out Her Scenes in ‘Amazing Spider-Man 2’ Were Cut: The Role of Mary Jane Was ‘My Dream’
articles.summary: More than 12 years later, Shailene Woodley has opened up about her disappointment in finding out that her part in “The Amazing Spider-Man 2” opposite Andrew Garfield didn’t make the final cut.
body: Woodley said she was also told, “’Let’s wait for [Gwen Stacy] to die and then we’ll introduce Mary Jane.’ Which made sense. But then they didn’t make that film.”

In 2014, at the New York premiere of “The Amazing Spider-Man 2” (which featured a Mary Jane-themed cocktail ), producer Matt Tolmach told Variety this about the deletion of Woodley’s scenes: “We bit off more story than we could tell. We had a 148-page script. We were in the middle of that, and we realized this story [with Mary Jane] is not going to be in this movie.”
In Sam Raimi’s Spider-Man movie trilogy, the role of Mary Jane was played by Kirsten Dunst opposite Tobey Maguire.

In Woodley’s nearly 90-minute “SAG-AFTRA Foundation Conversations” interview, she also spoke about her performances in “Divergent,” “Dumb Money,” “The Descendants,” “The Fault in Our Stars,” HBO’s “Big Little Lies” and Season 2 of Hulu’s “Paradise.”

articles.title: How 'Book Queen' Dolly Parton inspired millions of children with gift of reading
articles.summary: Families across the globe share how free books from Parton's Imagination Library helped their children.
body: Across the globe in Australia, a toddler with speech delays delighted her family with her first word - "orange" - after she and her twin sister received a free book in the post about colours. It came from Imagination Library, the literacy programme begun by late global superstar Dolly Parton.

Parton, who died this week aged 80, launched the philanthropic effort in 1995 to honour her father - whose difficult Appalachian upbringing never allowed him to finish school or learn to read and write.

"He was the smartest man I have ever known, but I know in my heart his inability to read probably kept him from fulfilling all of his dreams," wrote Parton in an open letter on Imagination Library's website.

Imagination Library sends one free book a month to children from birth to age five. It first launched in Tennessee's Sevier County, where Parton grew up, before expanding across the US in 2000. The programme, which partners with local organisations, launched in Canada in 2006, the UK the following year, then Australia in 2013 and Ireland in 2019.

articles.title: Bill Maher Gives Unsavory Dolly Parton Tribute While Criticizing Media Coverage of Her Death
articles.summary: Another tribute, like Maher's, that drew negative attention was that of Ricky Schroder, who portrayed Parton's father in two biopic movies based on her childhood.
body: During the Friday episode of Real Time, Bill Maher addressed Dolly Parton’s death in an unsavory manner.

He began his monologue by discussing current events of the week, specifically the United States’ trade war with Canada. “All this is going on, and all America could really talk about this week was how sad it is we lost Dolly Parton,” Maher said.

Parton died Tuesday after a “brief battle with cancer,” a rep announced. Her death has sparked a plethora of tributes as people around the world have continued to honor her legacy. Among those who remembered Parton were Miley Cyrus, Taylor Swift, Beyoncé, Sabrina Carpenter, Billy Ray Cyrus and many more.

In a follow-up post after the backlash from his initial comments began, Schroder reportedly posted a clip on his Instagram Stories about the two-time Oscar nominee’s support of the COVID-19 vaccine, writing, “I warned Dolly to not support the Experiment. Wished she listened.”

articles.title: Charli XCX electrifies Reading Festival with era-spanning set
articles.summary: The British singer and Irish rock band Fontaines DC both headlined the first night of Reading for 2026.
body: Charli XCX has ushered in her next era with an electrifying headline set at Reading Festival which showcased hits from across her music career.

It marked the British singer's first UK festival performance since releasing her latest studio album - Music, Fashion, Film - which is a pivot from her culture-shaping, electronic-pop record Brat and features more of a rock edge.
But her Friday evening show highlighted the best of both, alongside fan favourite tracks from her back catalogue.

She also upped the production from her last Brat tour, with more elaborate staging, numerous costume changes, dramatic pyro and strobe lighting, and she was accompanied by a host of dancers and a live band.

articles.title: Milo Yiannopoulos in ICE Custody After Feud-Fueled Tip-Off
articles.summary: Laura Loomer, whom the far-right provocateur waged a vicious campaign against last year, says she reported the political operative's immigration status
body: Far-right provocateur Milo Yiannopoulos has been detained at an Immigration and Customs Enforcement facility in Louisiana and is awaiting deportation after allegedly overstaying his visa and remaining in the U.S. illegally.

Yiannopoulos lives in the United States, primarily in Los Angeles, but was born in and is a citizen of the U.K. He is currently registered in ICE’s detainee database, but there are scant details about his detention and where he is being held.
On Friday, the Department of Homeland Security posted a statement on X announcing Yiannopoulos’s detention.

“On August 27, ICE arrested Milo Yiannopoulos, an illegal alien from the United Kingdom, at the Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport (MSY) in Kenner, Louisiana,” the statement reads. “Yiannopoulos legally entered the country on May 14, 2019, through New York City, New York. He chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation’s laws.”

articles.title: ‘I don’t care if I look good’: French heartthrob Louis Garrel on fashion, fatherhood and his radically dorky new role
articles.summary: The star has long been French cinema’s favourite tousle-haired Adonis, which makes his latest performance – as a schlubby, stay-at-home dad – all the more surprising. ‘I appreciate people laughing at me,’ he says.
body: ‘E ven though I’ve been working in film for over 20 years, I still have this desire to look beautiful on screen,” says Louis Garrel, on a video call from his bed inside a boat off the coast of Corsica. The French film star is lying on his stomach, occasionally kicking up his bare legs, ruffling his curls and running the nail of his thumb over his moustache. I think the person he sees on the laptop screen in front of him is me, but I am pretty certain he is flirting with his own reflection.

The attraction between the Paris-born 43-year-old and the camera tends to be reciprocal. Long of limb, tousled of hair and chiselled of nose, Garrel has spent a career on screen as French cinema’s favourite Adonis – the man film-makers turn to when they need an erotic wrecking ball to smash up bourgeois twosomes and turn them into quivering menages a trois.

articles.title: Memo to Ridley Scott: no one needs more Alien: Covenant movies – get the franchise back to stalk’n’slash
articles.summary: News that Scott is working on a follow-up to his maligned 2017 film leaves me worried the franchise has run out of shocks. If any science-fiction saga looked beyond recovery, it was the Alien franchise.
body: And then in 2024, we got Fede Álvarez’s Alien: Romulus, in which actual xenomorphs chase actual human beings down actual corridors for the clearly defined purposes of either killing them or putting smaller xenomorphs inside them. Better still, a year later we got Noah Hawley’s Alien: Earth, which reminded us that giant, murderous space insects are in fact less awful than tech trillionaires.

It’s not the first time Scott has talked up sequels to Covenant. During the publicity run for the film, he said a follow-up was already being written and that he would start shooting within 14 months. He also suggested he could make as many as six more Alien prequels, with the series eventually leading up to the original Alien. Eight years and no prequels later, Scott announced that he had “done enough” with the franchise and merely hoped it would continue without him. Now he appears to have reverted to an earlier mode.
